questions.q: What is the central point of the passage?
options: Most people manage twenty-four hours well and should stop worrying about wasted time
Modern workers should abandon aspiration because it only produces constant discomfort
Many people feel an uneasy aspiration to do more than their obligations and never act on it
Pilgrimage and travel are the surest cure for feeling that years slip away
questions.explain: The author says a common uneasy feeling comes from wanting to exceed one's formal programme.

questions.q: What example does the author use of a man who desires to go to Mecca?
options: One who never leaves Brixton
One who is robbed at Port Said
One who goes by train to Paris
One who joins a pilgrimage group
questions.explain: He contrasts a traveler who sets out with the man who never leaves Brixton.

questions.q: Which thinker does the author call the greatest mind that ever lived?
options: Herbert Spencer
Immanuel Kant
Isaac Newton
John Stuart Mill
questions.explain: He calls Herbert Spencer the greatest mind that ever lived.

questions.q: What does the author say about literature?
options: It is the only dependable source for satisfying a hunger for learning
It is becoming too costly for ordinary clerks to enjoy regularly
It is not the only well for slaking the thirst for knowledge
It is overrated compared with newspapers and popular competitions
questions.explain: He says literature is not the only well and knowledge can be sought apart from it.

questions.q: What does the author imply about the person who says living on 24 hours is easy?
options: He is annoyed by such a person and wants him to stop boasting
He admires such a person and plans to copy his daily timetable
He believes such a person is common and needs no advice at all
He doubts such a person exists and would like to learn his secret
questions.explain: He says he has long wished to meet him and asks him to come forward, implying such people are rare.
